references.text: God's command not to have other gods and not to worship idols, which is the basis for Joshua's call to the people to choose whom they will serve.
Moses sets before the people the same choice between life and death, blessing and curse, urging them to choose life by loving the Lord.
Elijah challenges the people on Mount Carmel with similar words: 'How long will you limp along on both sides?' - a call to choose between the Lord and Baal.
Jacob commands his household to remove foreign gods, reflecting Joshua's call to discard the gods of their fathers from beyond the river.
Abraham's call to leave his land and his kindred, which is the background for 'the fathers who lived beyond the river' serving other gods.
Jesus teaches that no one can serve two masters, echoing Joshua's call to choose whom they will serve.
Paul writes about the choice between being slaves under sin or under righteousness, an echo of Joshua's call to choose whom they will serve.
The Lord's warning against being lukewarm, reflecting Joshua's demand for a clear choice and his own declaration that he and his household will serve the Lord.
